notes_list.title: Confer: Synonym
notes_list.basic_overview: CONFER (to discuss and decide together) is closest to 'negotiate'.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Wrong options in the same question were dishonor, refuse, corrupt. 'Confer' can also mean 'to bestow'.

notes_list.title: Burst: Phrasal Verbs
notes_list.basic_overview: Burst into = suddenly start doing something / start burning with large flames. The aircraft crashed and burst into flames.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Burst in = intrude and interrupt; burst on = appear suddenly and attract attention; burst out = suddenly start laughing or crying, or shout.

notes_list.title: Subject of / on / with; Subjected to
notes_list.basic_overview: Subject of = a subject belonging to something (Maths is my favourite subject of study). Subject on = a topic (He wrote a book on the subject of AI).
notes_list.extra_info_content: Subject with = used only when 'with' connects another thing (Bring the book on this subject with the blue cover; 'with' belongs to the book's cover, not the subject). Simple SOP: if you see 'subjected', put 'to'. If only 'subject' appears, pause and check the meaning of the sentence.

notes_list.title: Spelling Rules
notes_list.basic_overview: Adding -ly keeps the base word (public + ly = publicly). Adding -ance drops the silent e (guide + ance = guidance).
notes_list.extra_info_content: Watch ei vs ie (receive, believe) and a vs e (guidance, not guidence). Break words into parts (gov-ern-ment) so silent letters are not missed.
